# Appendix H: The grammar

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_appendix_h.py from book/appendices/appendix-h.template.md, spec/grammar.md and spec/type-system.md §15.2; edit those, not this page. -->

This appendix lists the grammar of CeeSafe %ceesafec-version%: what the parser of `ceesafec` accepts, as productions. Use it to
settle a question of form, such as where a comma may go or which operator binds tighter, and follow the links
beside each group to the section that teaches the form with examples.

The productions are copied from the specification, character for character, and are not rewritten here: all but
the last block are the productions of
[the grammar](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/grammar) (`spec/grammar.md`), in its order, and the
block under [Patterns](#patterns) is from
[the type system, §15.2](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/type-system) (`spec/type-system.md`). A form
that no production here derives is rejected by the parser. A form that a production derives may still be rejected
by a later check, such as type checking or the borrow rule, which the chapters teach.

## How to read this notation

The notation is EBNF. One production defines one name:

| Notation | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Name = …` | The production that defines `Name`. A name with a capital first letter is defined by a production, or is a token of the [lexical grammar](#lexical-grammar). |
| `'x'` | The token `x`, written as it is in a source file. `'fn'` is the keyword `fn`, and `'('` is an opening parenthesis. |
| `A B` | `A`, then `B`. |
| `A \| B` | `A` or `B`. A line that begins with `\|` continues the production above it with one more alternative. |
| `X?` | `X` or nothing. |
| `X*` | `X` zero or more times. |
| `X+` | `X` one or more times. |
| `( … )` | A group, so that `?`, `*`, `+` or `\|` applies to all of it. `('->' Type)?` is an optional result type. |
| `'a'..'z'` | In the lexical grammar, any one character from `a` to `z`. |
| `(* … *)` | A comment. In the patterns block a comment begins with `--` and runs to the end of the line. |

Three things in the comments are not part of the form:

- A tag such as `M2d`, `L1`, `C7a` or `G5` names the step of the compiler's history that added the form. It has
  no meaning for a program.
- `ADR 0085 §2.3` names a decision of the specification, a page under
  [decisions](https://ceesafe.github.io/CeeSafe/reference/decisions/).
- `type-system.md §36.1`, or a bare `§21`, names the section of the type system that gives the form its rules.

`EOF` is the end of the file. `StringLiteral` and `CharLiteral` are tokens: their forms are described in prose
under [Strings and characters](#strings-and-characters).

## Lexical grammar

A source file is UTF-8 text. The lexer turns it into tokens. Whitespace and comments separate tokens and are then
discarded, except that a `///` comment is kept as documentation for the declaration that follows it.
[Comments](./ch03-04-comments) teaches both kinds of comment.

### Identifiers and keywords

```text
Identifier = IdentStart IdentContinue*      (not a keyword)
IdentStart = 'A'..'Z' | 'a'..'z' | '_'
IdentContinue = IdentStart | '0'..'9'
```

A lone `_` is a token of its own, not an identifier. The keywords are all reserved: none can be a name, whether
or not the language uses it yet.

```text
as borrow break const continue defer drop else enum extern false fn for if impl
import in interface internal let loop match move mut namespace null own private
public return Self static struct this true type unsafe using var where while
class async await yield macro
```

The names of the primitive types, such as `i32`, `u64`, `bool` and `void`, are identifiers and not keywords. Four
more words have a meaning in one place only and are identifiers everywhere else: `is` after a complete operand,
`region` before a name in a list of type parameters, `dyn` in a type, and `union` in an `extern` block.
[Variables](./ch03-01-variables) teaches names, and [Data types](./ch03-02-data-types) the primitive types.

### Numbers

```text
IntLiteral = (Decimal | '0x' HexDigits | '0b' BinDigits | '0o' OctDigits) IntSuffix?
IntSuffix  = 'i8'|'i16'|'i32'|'i64'|'isize'|'u8'|'u16'|'u32'|'u64'|'usize'
Decimal    = Digit ('_'? Digit)*                (* HexDigits, BinDigits and OctDigits likewise, with their digits *)
Digit      = '0'..'9'
```

```text
FloatLiteral = Decimal '.' Decimal Exponent? FloatSuffix? | Decimal Exponent FloatSuffix?
Exponent = ('e'|'E') ('+'|'-')? Decimal
FloatSuffix = 'f32' | 'f64'
```

`1.` and `.5` are not float literals, and `1..2` is the three tokens `1`, `..` and `2`. A decimal literal may
begin with zeros, and `010` is ten. [Data types](./ch03-02-data-types) teaches the literals and their suffixes.

### Strings and characters

The specification describes these in prose, not in productions:

| Form | What it is |
|---|---|
| `"text"` | A string literal, on one line. Its escapes are `\n`, `\r`, `\t`, `\\`, `\"`, `\'`, `\0`, `\{`, `\}` and `\u{…}` with one to six hexadecimal digits. |
| `"""` to `"""` | A raw string literal of several lines. The opening `"""` ends its line. The content is the lines that follow, up to a line that holds only spaces or tabs and then `"""`. That closing line's indentation is removed from every line. There are no escapes. |
| `c"text"` | A C string literal, with the escapes of `"text"` except `\0`. The compiler adds the NUL byte at its end. |
| `'c'` | A character literal: one Unicode scalar value or one escape. Its value is an integer. |

[Strings and string views](./ch08-02-strings) teaches string literals, and
[Calling C and being called by it](./ch20-02-calling-c) the C string literal.

### Punctuation and operators

```text
( ) { } [ ] , ; : . .. ..= @ ? ?? -> =>
+ - * / % ! & | ^ ~ && || << 
= == != < <= > >=
+= -= *= /= %= &= |= ^= <<=
```

The lexer never makes a `>>` or `>>=` token. The parser reads two `>` that touch as the shift operator, and a
`>` that touches a `>=` as `>>=`, so that the end of `Vector<Box<Point>>` is two closing brackets. `..=` is a token
of patterns only, and `??` is two `?` when it is read in a type. Any character that starts no token is the error
N0001.

## Items

A file is a list of items: the declarations at its top level. There is no statement outside a function.

### A file

```text
CompilationUnit = NamespaceDecl? ImportDecl* Item* EOF
NamespaceDecl   = 'namespace' QualifiedName ';'     (* retired by ADR 0013: accepted, no effect *)
ImportDecl      = 'import' Identifier ('.' Identifier)? ';'   (* M10 T5: a dependency, or one of its items; type-system.md §2 *)
QualifiedName   = Identifier ('.' Identifier)*
```

[Imports](./ch07-03-imports) teaches `import`. A `namespace` line is accepted and has no effect.

### Items, attributes and the declarations with type parameters

```text
Item       = Attribute* Visibility? (FunctionDecl | ConstDecl | StaticDecl | StructDecl | EnumDecl | InterfaceDecl
                                     | ImplDecl | ExternBlock)
Attribute  = '@' Identifier ('(' AttributeArg (',' AttributeArg)* ')')?   (* M8b; type-system.md §28.1 *)
AttributeArg = Identifier | StringLiteral | IntLiteral
ExternBlock = 'extern' StringLiteral '{' (ExternFn | ExternStruct | ExternUnion | ExternEnum | ExternConst | ExternStatic)* '}'  (* M8b; §28.2 *)
ExternStruct = Attribute* Visibility? 'struct' Identifier ('{' (ExternField | AnonymousUnion)* '}' | ';')   (* C6b; type-system.md §31 *)
ExternUnion = Attribute* Visibility? 'union' Identifier ('{' ExternField+ '}' | ';')   (* ADR 0041; type-system.md §31.1 *)
ExternEnum = Attribute* Visibility? 'enum' Identifier ':' Type ';'   (* ADR 0079; type-system.md §31.6 *)
ExternConst = Attribute* Visibility? 'const' Identifier ':' Type ('=' Expr)? ';'   (* ADR 0080; type-system.md §28.2 *)
ExternStatic = Attribute* Visibility? 'static' 'mut'? Identifier ':' Type ';'   (* ADR 0080; type-system.md §39.6 *)
AnonymousUnion = 'union' '{' ExternField+ '}'                               (* ADR 0041: a C11 anonymous union member *)
ExternField = Attribute* FieldDecl                                           (* C9: @cname; type-system.md §31.1 *)
ExternFn   = Attribute* Visibility? 'fn' Identifier '(' (Param (',' Param)* (',' '...')? ','?)? ')' ('->' Type)? ';'   (* `...`: ADR 0041 *)
TypeParams = '<' TypeParam (',' TypeParam)* '>'               (* M6a; type-system.md §20 *)
InterfaceDecl = 'interface' Identifier TypeParams? (':' Type ('+' Type)*)? '{' (MethodSig | InterfaceConst | AssocTypeDecl)* '}'
                                            (* M6b; §21; supertraits: ADR 0086 §2.6 *)
InterfaceConst = 'const' Identifier ':' Type ('=' Expr)? ';'   (* ADR 0086 §2.4: the value is a default *)
AssocTypeDecl = 'type' Identifier (':' Type ('+' Type)*)? ';'   (* ADR 0086 §2.5 *)
MethodSig  = Attribute* 'fn' Identifier TypeParams? '(' ParamList? ')' ('->' Type)? (';' | FunctionBody)
                                            (* attributes: M13 G2, `@effects`, §37.3; a FunctionBody is a default, ADR 0086 §2.1 *)
ImplDecl   = 'impl' TypeParams? Type 'for' Type '{' (Attribute* 'public'? FunctionDecl | ConstDecl | AssocTypeDef)* '}'
                                            (* M6b; §21; TypeParams: ADR 0054; attributes C7a; ConstDecl and
                                               AssocTypeDef: ADR 0086 §2.4, §2.5; `public` has no effect, and no other
                                               modifier is accepted: ADR 0109 §2.5 *)
           | 'impl' TypeParams? Type '{' (Attribute* Visibility? FunctionDecl | Visibility? ConstDecl)* '}'
                                            (* inherent: ADR 0064 §1; §21.1; ConstDecl: ADR 0074 §2.7, and N0216 in an
                                               impl with TypeParams *)
AssocTypeDef = 'type' Identifier '=' Type ';'
MemberCall = Expr '.' Identifier ('<' GenericArg (',' GenericArg)* '>')? '(' ArgList? ')'   (* type arguments: ADR 0064 §1 *)
TypeParam  = 'region' Identifier (':' Identifier ('+' Identifier)*)?
                                                               (* M6x: a region, before any type parameter; §25.1.
                                                                  Its bounds, the regions it outlives: ADR 0134,
                                                                  type-system.md §25.8. The parser reads a Type
                                                                  for each; one that is not a region parameter's
                                                                  name is N0273 *)
           | 'const' Identifier ':' Type                       (* ADR 0083: a const parameter; type-system.md §20.5 *)
           | Identifier (':' Type ('+' Type)*)?                (* bounds: M6b *)
(* `region` is contextual: only `region` followed by a name declares a region. In a type, a region
   argument is a region name or `static`, written first in the argument list (`Token<src>`,
   `StringView<r>`, `Slice<r, T>`) or in `borrow(r) T`; type-system.md §25.2. *)
EnumDecl   = 'enum' Identifier TypeParams? '{' (Variant (',' Variant)* ','?)? '}'        (* M2d *)
Variant    = ('@' 'from')? Identifier ('(' Type (',' Type)* ','? ')')?   (* `@from`: ADR 0075 §2.3 *)
Visibility = 'public' | 'internal' | 'private'
```

| Form | Taught in |
|---|---|
| `Visibility`: `public`, `internal`, `private` | [Files and public](./ch07-02-files-and-public) |
| `Attribute`: `@test`, `@derive(…)`, `@export("name")` | [How to write tests](./ch11-01-writing-tests), [Derives and macros](./ch20-05-derives-and-macros) |
| `ExternBlock` and what it declares | [Calling C and being called by it](./ch20-02-calling-c) |
| `TypeParams`, `TypeParam` with bounds | [Generic types and functions](./ch10-01-generic-types) |
| `TypeParam` that begins `region` | [Regions](./ch10-03-regions) |
| `TypeParam` that begins `const` | [More on interfaces and generics](./ch20-03-more-interfaces-and-generics) |
| `InterfaceDecl`, `MethodSig`, `ImplDecl` | [Interfaces](./ch10-02-interfaces) |
| `InterfaceConst`, `AssocTypeDecl`, `AssocTypeDef`, an interface after `:` | [More on interfaces and generics](./ch20-03-more-interfaces-and-generics) |
| `impl` with no interface | [Methods](./ch05-03-methods) |
| `EnumDecl`, `Variant` | [Defining an enum](./ch06-01-defining-an-enum) |
| `Variant` with `@from` | [Result, ? and !](./ch09-02-result) |

### Functions

```text
FunctionDecl = 'unsafe'? 'async'? 'fn' Identifier TypeParams? '(' ParamList? ')' ('->' Type)? FunctionBody
                                            (* 'unsafe': M8a; 'async': L1, type-system.md §40, ADR 0031 *)
ParamList    = (Receiver | Param) (',' Param)* ','?
Receiver     = ('borrow' 'mut'?)? 'this'   (* M2a: by value; M2b: reference receivers *)
Param        = Identifier ':' Type
```

[Functions](./ch03-03-functions) teaches the declaration, and [Methods](./ch05-03-methods) the receiver `this`.
[Unsafe code](./ch20-01-unsafe-code) teaches `unsafe fn`, and [Tasks and await](./ch17-01-tasks-and-await)
`async fn`.

### Structs

```text
StructDecl   = 'struct' Identifier TypeParams? '{' Member* '}'          (* M2a; TypeParams M6a *)
Member       = Visibility? FieldDecl | Attribute* Visibility? FunctionDecl | DropBlock   (* method attributes: C7a, type-system.md §32 *)
             | Visibility? ConstDecl                                (* ADR 0074 §2.7: an associated constant, type-system.md §10 *)
DropBlock    = 'drop' Block                (* M2c *)
FieldDecl    = Identifier ':' Type ';'
FunctionBody = Block | '=>' Expr ';'
```

[Defining and making structs](./ch05-01-defining-structs) teaches fields, [Methods](./ch05-03-methods) the
functions in a struct's body, and [Destruction](./ch15-02-destruction) the `drop` block. A `FunctionBody` that
is `=>` and an expression is taught in [Functions](./ch03-03-functions).

### Constants and statics

```text
ConstDecl = 'const' Identifier ':' Type '=' Expr ';'
StaticDecl = 'static' 'mut'? Identifier ':' Type '=' Expr ';'   (* M14 K1; type-system.md §39 *)
```

[Variables](./ch03-01-variables) teaches `const`, and [Kernel code](./ch22-02-kernel-code) teaches `static`
and `static mut`.

## Types

```text
Type = QualifiedName
     | 'borrow' 'mut'? Sources? Type          (* M2b references; Sources only in return types *)
     | '[' Type ';' Expr ']'                   (* M2d fixed array; the length: type-system.md §16.1, ADR 0083 §2.7 *)
     | ('Slice' | 'SliceMut') '<' Type '>'     (* M2d slices *)
     | 'Result' '<' Type ',' Type '>'          (* M3a; type-system.md §17 *)
     | Type '?'                                (* M6c: optional; `borrow T?` is an optional reference *)
     | '(' Type ')'                            (* M11 (G6): `borrow (T?)` is a reference to an optional *)
     | Attribute* 'fn' '(' (Type (',' Type)*)? ')' ('->' Type)?   (* M11 (G8a): a function value, type-system.md §36.1;
                                               G8b′: `@effects(…)` before `fn`, §36.3 *)
     | Identifier '<' GenericArg (',' GenericArg)* '>'   (* M6a: an instantiation of a generic struct or enum; also
                                                  Box, Pool, … *)
     | 'extern' StringLiteral 'fn' '(' (Type (',' Type)*)? ')' ('->' Type)?   (* M8d: a pointer to a C function,
                                                  `extern "C" fn(i32) -> i32`; type-system.md §29.5 *)
     | '*' 'mut'? Type                         (* M8a: raw pointer; type-system.md §27 *)
     | 'dyn' Type DynMarker*                   (* M13 G2: an interface instantiation; only behind `borrow` or in
                                                  `Box<…>`; type-system.md §37. `dyn` is a keyword only here *)
     | 'dyn' 'mut'? Attribute* 'fn' '(' (Type (',' Type)*)? ')' ('->' Type)? DynMarker*
                                               (* M13 G3: an owning closure's type, §36.5 *)
DynMarker = '+' ('Send' | 'Share')               (* type-system.md §38.4; `Share`: ADR 0084 §2.5 *)
Sources = '(' Source (',' Source)* ')'           (* only if a type follows the ')'; else '(' Type ')' *)
Source  = Identifier | 'this' | 'static'         (* a parameter, the receiver, or a region (type-system.md §25.2) *)
GenericArg = Type | ConstArg                     (* ADR 0083; type-system.md §20.5 *)
ConstArg   = 'true' | 'false' | IntLiteral | '(' Expr ')'
           (* a name or `E.V` parses as a Type; the parameter's kind decides (N0354). `'(' Expr ')'` only in a type:
              a `(` that a type follows (`(borrow T)`, `(*T)`, `(fn …)`, `(dyn I)`, `(T?)`, `(T)?`) is a Type *)
```

The alternative that begins `'extern'` is `extern "C" fn(A) -> R`, a pointer to a C function, which
[Calling C and being called by it](./ch20-02-calling-c) teaches.

| Form | Taught in |
|---|---|
| A name: `i32`, `Point`, `Self.Item` | [Data types](./ch03-02-data-types) |
| `borrow T`, `borrow mut T` | [Borrowing](./ch04-02-borrowing) |
| `borrow(a, b) T`, with `Sources` | [Regions](./ch10-03-regions) |
| `[T; n]` | [Data types](./ch03-02-data-types) |
| `Slice<T>`, `SliceMut<T>` | [Slices and views](./ch04-03-slices-and-views) |
| `Result<T, E>` | [Result, ? and !](./ch09-02-result) |
| `T?` | [Optionals](./ch06-03-optionals) |
| `fn(A) -> R`, `dyn fn(A) -> R`, `dyn mut fn()` | [Closures](./ch13-01-closures) |
| `Vector<T>`, with `GenericArg` | [Generic types and functions](./ch10-01-generic-types) |
| `ConstArg` | [More on interfaces and generics](./ch20-03-more-interfaces-and-generics) |
| `*T`, `*mut T` | [Unsafe code](./ch20-01-unsafe-code) |
| `dyn I` | [Dynamic dispatch](./ch18-01-dynamic-dispatch) |

## Statements

```text
Block = '{' Statement* '}'
Statement = Block
          | LocalDecl
          | IfStmt
          | 'while' '(' Expr ')' Block
          | 'loop' Block
          | 'break' ';'
          | 'continue' ';'
          | 'return' Expr? ';'
          | 'using' Identifier (':' Type)? '=' Expr ';'      (* M2c *)
          | 'defer' Statement                               (* M2c *)
          | MatchStmt                                       (* M2d; type-system.md §15.2 *)
          | 'for' '(' Identifier 'in' Expr ('..' Expr)? ')' Block   (* M2d; type-system.md §16.4 *)
          | 'unsafe' Block                                  (* M8a; type-system.md §27.4 *)
          | Expr AssignOp Expr ';'        (* assignment: a statement, not an expression *)
          | Expr ';'
LocalDecl = ('let' | 'var') Identifier (':' Type)? ('=' Expr)? ';'
          | 'let' '_' '=' Expr ';'          (* ADR 0072: evaluates Expr and destroys its value, as `Expr;` *)
          | 'let' Pattern '=' Expr 'else' Block ';'   (* ADR 0117; type-system.md §15.5: Block must leave *)
          | 'let' StructPattern '=' Expr ';'          (* ADR 0123; §15.5: the pattern cannot fail *)
IfStmt    = 'if' '(' Expr ')' Block ('else' (IfStmt | Block))?
AssignOp  = '=' | '+=' | '-=' | '*=' | '/=' | '%=' | '&=' | '|=' | '^=' | '<<=' | '>>='
```

Braces are required after `if`, `else`, `while` and `loop`. An assignment is a statement and not an expression,
so `if (x = 1)` is a syntax error. `MatchStmt` is defined with the [patterns](#patterns).

| Form | Taught in |
|---|---|
| `LocalDecl`: `let`, `var`, `let _ =` | [Variables](./ch03-01-variables) |
| `let Pattern = Expr else Block;` | [Where patterns go](./ch19-01-where-patterns-go) |
| `IfStmt`, `while`, `loop`, `break`, `continue`, `for` | [Control flow](./ch03-05-control-flow) |
| `for` over a collection or an iterator | [Iteration](./ch13-02-iteration) |
| `return` | [Functions](./ch03-03-functions) |
| `MatchStmt` | [match](./ch06-02-match) |
| `using`, `defer` | [Destruction](./ch15-02-destruction) |
| `unsafe` block | [Unsafe code](./ch20-01-unsafe-code) |
| `AssignOp` | [Variables](./ch03-01-variables), [Arithmetic](./ch20-04-arithmetic) |

## Expressions

### Precedence

The binary and prefix operators are not in the productions: this table gives them, from the loosest binding to
the tightest. Every binary level associates to the left, except that the comparisons do not associate at all
(`a < b < c` is the error N0103) and `??` associates to the right.

| Level | Operators | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `??` | right-assoc, short-circuit (ADR 0072; type-system.md §22.1). An unparenthesised `\|\|` or `&&` operand beside it is N0100 |
| 1 | `\|\|` | short-circuit |
| 2 | `&&` | short-circuit |
| 3 | `== != < <= > >=`, `is` | non-associative. `e is P` (ADR 0085 §2.8; type-system.md §15.4): after `is` the pattern grammar reads as far as it can, so a `\|` there is an or-pattern: `(c is 'a') \| flag` needs the parentheses |
| 4 | `\|` | |
| 5 | `^` | |
| 6 | `&` | |
| 7 | `<< >>` | |
| 8 | `+ -` | |
| 9 | `* / %` | |
| 10 | `as` | `Expr 'as' Type`, left-assoc (`x as u32 as u64`). A primitive type name (`u8` … `u64`, `i8` … `i64`, `usize`, `isize`, `f32`, `f64`, `bool`, `char`) takes no type arguments, so `a as u64 < b` is `(a as u64) < b` (ADR 0075 §2.13) |
| 11 | unary `- !`, `*` (ADR 0075 §2.14: reading through a reference), `borrow`, `borrow mut`, `move`; `await` (L1) | prefix, right-assoc (`- -x`); `await`'s operand: below |
| 12 | postfix: call `(...)`, member `.name`, index and slice `[...]`, `?` (propagate), `!` (unwrap) | left to right: `Postfix` below |

The bit operators bind tighter than the comparisons, so `x & 1 == 0` is `(x & 1) == 0`.
[Data types](./ch03-02-data-types) teaches the arithmetic and comparison operators,
[Arithmetic](./ch20-04-arithmetic) the bit operators, the shifts and `as`, [Optionals](./ch06-03-optionals) `??`,
and [Where patterns go](./ch19-01-where-patterns-go) `is`.

### Primary and postfix expressions

```text
Primary = IntLiteral | FloatLiteral | StringLiteral | CharLiteral | 'true' | 'false' | 'null'
        | Identifier GenericArgs? | '(' Expr ')' | 'this'
        | 'Self' | 'Self' '{' FieldInits? '}'               (* ADR 0086 §2.2; §1.3 *)
        | 'unsafe' '{' Expr '}'                              (* M8a: an unsafe expression *)
        | IfExpr | MatchExpr                                 (* M11 (G5): type-system.md §15.3 *)
        | '(' (ClosureParam (',' ClosureParam)*)? ')' '=>' (Block | Expr)   (* M11 (G8b): a closure, §36.2 *)
        | 'move' '(' (ClosureParam (',' ClosureParam)*)? ')' '=>' (Block | Expr)   (* M13 G3: a move literal, §36.5 *)
        | 'async' 'move'? '(' (ClosureParam (',' ClosureParam)*)? ')' '=>' (Block | Expr)
                                                     (* L1: an async closure, §40.3; `move`: a child that owns what it
                                                        captures, §40.5, ADR 0033 *)
        | Identifier GenericArgs? '{' FieldInits? '}'       (* struct literal, M2a; GenericArgs M6a *)
        | '[' Expr (',' Expr)* ','? ']' | '[' Expr ';' IntLiteral ']'   (* array literals, M2d *)
        | '[' ']'                                    (* the empty slice, ADR 0075 §2.9 *)
        | '[' Expr ':' Expr (',' Expr ':' Expr)* ','? ']'   (* an array by index, in a static's initialiser:
                                                        type-system.md §39.4, ADR 0091 §2.3 *)
IsTest  = Operand 'is' Pattern                       (* level 3; Pattern: type-system.md §15.2, §15.4 *)
Operand = Expr                                       (* of levels 4 to 12: what a level 3 operator takes on its left *)
ClosureParam = Identifier (':' Type)?             (* a '(' … ')' followed by '=>' is a closure *)
IfExpr    = 'if' '(' Expr ')' Branch 'else' (IfExpr | Branch)
MatchExpr = 'match' '(' Expr ')' '{' (ValueArm (',' ValueArm)* ','?)? '}'
ValueArm  = Pattern Guard? '=>' Branch               (* Guard: type-system.md §15.2 *)
Guard     = 'if' '(' Expr ')'                        (* ADR 0085 §2.2; an `Arm` of a MatchStmt takes one too *)
Branch    = Expr | Block | ValueBlock                (* a Block branch must not complete *)
ValueBlock = '{' Statement* Expr '}'                 (* its last Expr has no ';' (ADR 0073 §2.3) *)
FieldInits = FieldInit (',' FieldInit)* ','?
FieldInit  = Identifier ':' Expr
GenericArgs = '<' GenericArg (',' GenericArg)* '>'   (* only when followed by '(', '.' or '{' — see below *)
Postfix = Primary ( '(' ArgList? ')' | '.' Identifier | '[' IndexOrRange ']'
                  | '?' | '!' )*                     (* M3a: propagate / unwrap a Result *)
IndexOrRange = Expr | Expr? '..' Expr?               (* M2d: element or slice *)
ArgList = Arg (',' Arg)* ','?
Arg     = 'mut' Expr | Expr                (* `mut x` for a `borrow mut` parameter, M2b *)
Await   = 'await' AwaitOperand ( '?' | '!' ) PostfixRest*         (* L1; type-system.md §40.2, ADR 0031 §3.1 *)
        | 'await' AwaitOperand
AwaitOperand = Primary ( '(' ArgList? ')' | '.' Identifier | '[' IndexOrRange ']' )*
PostfixRest  = '(' ArgList? ')' | '.' Identifier | '[' IndexOrRange ']' | '?' | '!'
```

`Operand`, in `IsTest`, is the expression to the left of `is`, which is an operator of level 3 in the table.
After a name, `<` begins generic
arguments only when the tokens up to the matching `>` can form types or const arguments and the `>` is followed
by `(`, `.`, `{`, `)`, `,`, `;` or `]`. Otherwise it is the less-than operator. A name followed directly by `{`
is a struct literal.

| Form | Taught in |
|---|---|
| Literals, array literals `[a, b]` and `[x; n]` | [Data types](./ch03-02-data-types) |
| `IfExpr`, `MatchExpr`, `Branch`, `ValueBlock` | [Control flow](./ch03-05-control-flow), [match](./ch06-02-match) |
| Struct literal, `FieldInits` | [Defining and making structs](./ch05-01-defining-structs) |
| A closure, `move` closure, `ClosureParam` | [Closures](./ch13-01-closures) |
| `async` closure | [Scopes](./ch17-02-scopes) |
| `Await` | [Tasks and await](./ch17-01-tasks-and-await) |
| Call, `ArgList`, `mut x` as an argument | [Functions](./ch03-03-functions), [Borrowing](./ch04-02-borrowing) |
| `GenericArgs` at a call | [Generic types and functions](./ch10-01-generic-types) |
| `IndexOrRange`: `a[i]`, `a[1..4]`, `a[..]` | [Slices and views](./ch04-03-slices-and-views) |
| Postfix `?` and `!` | [Result, ? and !](./ch09-02-result), [Optionals](./ch06-03-optionals) |
| `IsTest`, `Guard` | [Where patterns go](./ch19-01-where-patterns-go) |
| `unsafe { e }` | [Unsafe code](./ch20-01-unsafe-code) |

## Patterns

The grammar names `Pattern` and `MatchStmt` and leaves their productions to the type system, §15.2. This block
is that section's.

```text
MatchStmt = 'match' '(' Expr ')' '{' Arm* '}'
Arm       = Pattern Guard? '=>' Block ','?
Guard     = 'if' '(' Expr ')'                                      -- ADR 0085 §2.2
Pattern   = '|'? AltPattern ('|' AltPattern)*                     -- or-patterns: ADR 0085 §2.3
AltPattern = (Identifier '@')? PrimPattern                         -- `name @ P`: ADR 0085 §2.5
PrimPattern = '_' | Literal | 'true' | 'false' | 'null'
          | '(' Pattern ')'
          | 'var'? Identifier                                      -- a constant in scope, else a binding: ADR 0085 §2.6
          | Bound '..=' Bound | Bound '..' Bound                  -- ranges: ADR 0085 §2.4
          | QualifiedName ('(' Payload (',' Payload)* ')')?        -- E.V, E.V(x, _), Ok(E.A(x)) (M11)
          | StringLiteral                                          -- on a StringView or Slice<u8>: ADR 0085 §2.7
          | '[' (SliceItem (',' SliceItem)* ','?)? ']'             -- slices and arrays: ADR 0085 §2.7
          | StructPattern                                          -- structs: ADR 0123
Bound     = Literal | Identifier                                   -- a constant's name: ADR 0118
SliceItem = Pattern | '..' | Identifier '@' '..'                   -- at most one '..' (N0100)
StructPattern = QualifiedName '{' (FieldPattern ',')* (FieldPattern | '..' ','?)? '}'   -- '..': the fields not named
FieldPattern  = Identifier ':' Pattern | 'var'? Identifier         -- `x` is `x: x`, `var x` is `x: var x`
Literal   = IntLiteral | '-' IntLiteral | CharLiteral
Payload   = Binding | Pattern                                      -- a nested pattern: M11 (G1)
Binding   = Identifier | 'var' Identifier | '_'        -- 'var': M3c (§18.4)
```

Every line of `PrimPattern` that begins with `|` is one of its alternatives. A payload that is a single identifier
is a binding, unless the name is a constant in scope.

| Form | Taught in |
|---|---|
| `MatchStmt`, `Arm`, variant patterns, `_` | [match](./ch06-02-match) |
| `Some(x)` and `null` | [Optionals](./ch06-03-optionals) |
| Where a pattern may be written: `match`, `is`, `let … else` | [Where patterns go](./ch19-01-where-patterns-go) |
| Which patterns can fail, and what a `match` must cover | [Patterns that can fail](./ch19-02-patterns-that-can-fail) |
| Every form: literals, ranges, `\|`, `name @ P`, strings, slices, `Guard` | [The syntax, whole](./ch19-03-the-syntax-whole) |

## Limits

Nesting is limited to 1,000 levels in a file: blocks, types, patterns, unary operands and each link of a chain
such as `a.b.c` or `1 + 1 + 1` count as levels. Past the limit the parser reports N0110 once and stops reading
that file.
